issues.description: setuptools<82 pin added to core/setup.py runtime install_requires, not just dev/build extras
issues.detail: The cap `setuptools<82` is being added to a dependency block in `core/setup.py` that appears to be part of install_requires/extras shipped to end users. This is a CI/build workaround for mmcv (open-mmlab/mmcv#3325) and should not propagate into the runtime dependency surface of autogluon-core. Pinning setuptools downstream for every consumer is overly invasive — most installs do not need mmcv. Move this cap to the CI script(s) only, or scope it to the multimodal extra that actually needs mmcv.

issues.description: mmcv 2.1.0 installed with --no-build-isolation may pick up wrong build deps
issues.detail: Switching from `mim install mmcv==2.1.0` to `pip install mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation` means mmcv will be built against whatever torch/numpy/setuptools are already in the environment. If the ambient env doesn't have the expected torch ABI / Cython / numpy headers staged before this line, the build will either fail or silently link against the wrong torch. The script should explicitly ensure torch (and any build-time deps mmcv needs) are installed before this call, and ideally document why no-build-isolation is required.

issues.description: mmdet bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no rationale
issues.detail: The PR title/description is scoped to 'fix mmengine failure', but the mmdet version is silently bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0. mmdet minor bumps frequently change registry/config behavior and downstream multimodal tests could regress. Either revert to 3.2.0 (the minimal change) or call out in the PR description that 3.3.0 is required by the mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0 combination and confirm CI passed the multimodal object-detection suite.

issues.description: Install order: mmcv built before mmengine is present
issues.detail: mmengine is typically a runtime/build-time peer of mmcv. The new order installs `mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation` first and then `mmengine==0.10.7`. This usually works because mmengine isn't a hard build dep of mmcv, but for clarity and to mirror upstream documentation, install mmengine before mmcv. If something in mmcv's build script touches mmengine, current ordering will fail.

`build_pkg` in env_setup.sh already pins `setuptools<82`, and `core/setup.py` now also declares `setuptools<82`. The extra `python3 -m pip install "setuptools<82"` at the top of setup_mmcv is belt-and-suspenders. Not harmful, but worth either consolidating (one place) or leaving a comment that this is intentional because setup_mmcv may run in a fresh shell where build_pkg hasn't executed.

issues.description: FIXME comments link to upstream issue but lack a tracking mechanism
issues.detail: Two FIXME comments reference open-mmlab/mmcv#3325 to remove the cap once fixed. There's no internal tracking issue or owner, and the cap exists in three places (env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, core/setup.py). Recommend filing an internal tracking ticket and listing all three locations in its description so the revert is easy when upstream lands.

issues.description: Switch from git-pinned mmengine commit to PyPI wheel changes reproducibility profile
issues.detail: Previously mmengine was pinned to a specific commit (2e0ab7a) carrying a torch 2.5 fix. Switching to mmengine==0.10.7 from PyPI is fine if 0.10.7 includes that fix, but the PR description doesn't confirm this. Worth a one-line comment that 0.10.7 contains the torch 2.5 compatibility fix that was the original reason for the git pin, so a future reader doesn't accidentally downgrade.

positions.position: Adding it to core/setup.py is the simplest way to guarantee fresh installs of autogluon don't hit the same mmcv build failure. CI green now, fix later.

core/setup.py defines the package's contract with users. A transient upstream CI bug must not leak into runtime install_requires for every autogluon-core consumer. The cap belongs in CI scripts and/or the multimodal extra only.

--no-build-isolation is fragile: mmcv will compile against whatever happens to be in the environment, which is exactly the class of failure that broke CI in the first place. Prefer using mim or building in an isolated env with explicitly pinned build deps.
mim is itself broken by the upstream setuptools>=82 / pkg_resources removal; using pip with --no-build-isolation while pinning setuptools<82 is the minimum-diff path that unblocks CI today.
Stay on 3.2.0; the PR is supposed to be scoped to mmengine/mmcv only, and an mmdet bump expands the blast radius.
mmdet 3.3.0 may be the version that actually pairs with mmcv 2.1.0 + mmengine 0.10.7 on current torch. If CI shows 3.2.0 fails with this stack, 3.3.0 is the right pin.

review.summary: The PR is a reasonable CI unblock for the upstream setuptools>=82 / pkg_resources removal that broke mmcv builds. The CI-only changes (env_setup.sh and setup_mmcv.sh) are pragmatic, though the switch to `--no-build-isolation` plus an undocumented mmdet bump (3.2.0 -> 3.3.0) widens the change beyond what the title implies and warrants confirmation that the multimodal object-detection CI suite still passes. The most concerning change is adding `setuptools<82` to core/setup.py's dependency list — that leaks a transient CI workaround into every downstream autogluon-core install and should be scoped to CI or to the multimodal extra. Recommend: (1) move the setuptools cap out of core/setup.py runtime deps, (2) add a one-line comment confirming mmengine 0.10.7 carries the torch 2.5 fix the prior git pin existed for, (3) file a tracking issue listing all three locations that need to be reverted when upstream mmcv#3325 is resolved.
